articles.title: Payments are where AI-built apps stop: seven things to wire before launch
articles.excerpt: Every AI-built app I have finished in the last year had the same shape. The screens look right, the database reads and writes, the demo runs on a laptop. Then someone tries to pay, and the project sto…
articles.body: Every AI-built app I have finished in the last year had the same shape. The screens look right, the database reads and writes, the demo runs on a laptop. Then someone tries to pay, and the project stops. Not because payments are hard to code. Because a payment is the first thing in the app that has to be correct in a way nobody can see from the outside: money leaves one account, lands in another, and either side can be wrong for days before anyone notices. Here are the seven things I wire, in this order, before a build is allowed to take a real card. Most of them are one afternoon of work. All of them are the reason a launch stays quiet instead of becoming a refund week. 1.

articles.title: CBOR Web Tokens: make cnf validation a proof test, not a claim lookup
articles.excerpt: CBOR Web Tokens: make cnf validation a proof test, not a claim lookup A confirmation claim can look deceptively simple. The issuer places a cnf key in a CBOR Web Token (CWT), and the receiver is suppo…
articles.body: CBOR Web Tokens: make cnf validation a proof test, not a claim lookup A confirmation claim can look deceptively simple. The issuer places a cnf key in a CBOR Web Token (CWT), and the receiver is supposed to know that the presenter has a particular key. RFC 8747 defines this proof-of-possession pattern for CWTs, while RFC 8392 defines the base token format. Parsing both specifications correctly is only the beginning of enforcement. The receiver must first validate the CWT signature, issuer, audience, expiration, and intended use. It should then read cnf as a CBOR map with the expected member types. The confirmation method determines what has to happen next. A key identifier might be used to locate a public key, but a key identifier does not prove possession.

articles.title: Show DEV: An Open 20-Asset Prompt Planner & Validation Toolkit for MAGI-2 Video Generation
articles.excerpt: I wanted to be able to reopen a video job and see exactly which picture defined a character, which clip supplied a camera move, and when a sound was supposed to land. A prompt pasted into a browser on…
articles.body: I wanted to be able to reopen a video job and see exactly which picture defined a character, which clip supplied a camera move, and when a sound was supposed to land. A prompt pasted into a browser only gave me part of that record. I settled on a small JSON job file that I can read in a diff and validate from a terminal before opening the generation interface. The problem A MAGI-2 omni-reference job can use up to 20 references, split across ten images, five videos, and five audio clips. That split matters. Six clips of camera movement exceed the video allowance even when every other slot is empty. The planner also has a 20,000-character script budget. I treat that number as a toolkit constraint and check separately what the generation endpoint actually accepts.

articles.body: 공포 탐욕 지수는 12에 머물고 있다. 24시간 만에 1.79% 하락한 2.12조 달러 규모의 시장에서 '극심한 공포'를 말해주는 수치다. 이 정도면 시장이 자기 인프라를 믿고 있다고 볼 수 있을까? 내 눈에는 그저 불안정한 모습으로 비친다. 수년 동안, 특히 마운트곡스 같은 대형 사건들이 터진 후 업계는 투명성을 갈구했다. 많은 이들이 '준비금 증명(PoR, Proof of Reserves)'이 해답이라고 믿었다. 암호화폐의 본질과도 잘 맞아떨어지는, 우아한 해결책처럼 들렸다. 거래소가 주장하는 자산을 실제로 보유하고 있음을 암호학적으로 증명한다니, 참 매력적이지 않은가. 하지만 우리는 여전히 깊은 신뢰 문제에 허덕이고 있다. 왜 그럴까? 이 업계를 30년간 지켜본 내 경험으로는, PoR이 일반적으로 구현되는 방식이 수탁형 금융 시스템에서 '신뢰'의 본질을 근본적으로 오해하고 있기 때문이다. 이 분석 글을 쓰는 데 있어, 특정 사실이나 숫자, 날짜에 대한 구체적인 출처 문서를 참고하지 않았다는 점을 미리 밝힌다. 이는 내 전반적인 전문 지식을 바탕으로 잘 알려진 업계 사건들과 기술 개념들을 논한다는 의미이며, 평소처럼 특정 수치나 인용문을 제시할 수는 없다는 뜻이다. 역설적이게도 이런 제약이, 우리가 지금 논하는 문제의 핵심, 즉 이 분야에서 검증 가능하고 포괄적인 정보를 얻기 어렵다는 사실을 더욱 명확히 보여준다고 생각한다. 내 관점은 이렇다. 준비금 증명이 실패한 건 암호학적 원리 자체에 결함이 있어서가 아니다. 시스템적인 문제에 대한 부분적인 해결책이었기 때문이다.

articles.title: Zanzibar consistency tokens: when an authorization read must wait
articles.excerpt: Zanzibar consistency tokens: when an authorization read must wait Authorization answers are data. They depend on relation tuples and other policy state that can change while a request is in flight. Go…
articles.body: Zanzibar consistency tokens: when an authorization read must wait Authorization answers are data. They depend on relation tuples and other policy state that can change while a request is in flight. Google's Zanzibar design uses consistency tokens, often called zookies, to connect a content update with a later permission check. The token is not a credential. It is a statement about how fresh the authorization read must be. The classic failure is easy to describe. A user loses access to a document, but a permission service still reads an old ACL and allows the user to view new content. Retrying with an older token does not fix that.
articles.author: johnettagaweraks

articles.title: Data Integrity proofs: verificationMethod and proofPurpose both carry authority
articles.excerpt: Data Integrity proofs: verificationMethod and proofPurpose both carry authority A signature over a Verifiable Credential or other structured document does not prove everything by itself. W3C Data Inte…
articles.body: Data Integrity proofs: verificationMethod and proofPurpose both carry authority A signature over a Verifiable Credential or other structured document does not prove everything by itself. W3C Data Integrity separates the cryptographic proof from the authority expressed by the document. Two fields are especially easy to under-check: verificationMethod identifies the key material, and proofPurpose states what relationship the proof is meant to establish. A verifier should resolve the verification method from a trusted controller document, confirm that it belongs to the expected controller, and confirm that the method is authorized for the stated purpose. An assertion method used to make claims is not automatically an authentication method.

articles.title: Venus shines at its brightest in the predawn sky this week. Here's where to look
articles.excerpt: Venus reaches peak brightness in the predawn sky this week, here's how to find it.
articles.body: Venus is at its most dazzling in the predawn sky this week as it shines close to the bright star Spica in the southeast. Here's what you need to know. As an inner planet, Venus never strays far from the horizon, at least compared to outer planets like Jupiter and Mars which can be visible all night long during opposition, when they shine opposite the sun in Earth's sky. Instead, Venus alternates between morning and evening appearances. All the while, its shifting moon-like phases and ever-changing proximity to Earth causes its brightness to wax and wane. When is Venus at its most dazzling? Venus will reach peak brightness during its current morning apparition at 1:37 p.m. EST (1837 GMT) on Nov. 27 according to the astronomy website In-The-Sky . articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 26, 2011: NASA's 2-ton nuclear-powered Curiosity rover launches to Mars
articles.excerpt: On November 26, 2011, the NASA Curiosity rover launched to Mars. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On November 26, 2011, the NASA Curiosity rover launched to Mars. The Mars rover Curiosity was the biggest and most powerful rover anyone had ever sent to the Red Planet. The 2-ton science laboratory is about the size of a small SUV. The mission's goal was to search for habitable environments on Mars , or evidence that the planet could have been habitable in the past. It launched on an Atlas V rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. About nine months later, Curiosity made a challenging landing on Mars. It successfully used a new landing technology called a sky crane to gently lower it to the surface. NASA's Curiosity rover lifts off atop a United Launch Alliance Atlas V rocket on Nov. 26, 2011 from Florida's Cape Canaveral Air Force Station.
